title: Supported coordinate product and proper projection recursion
statement: Fix a finite coefficient datum $P$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, with $A=A_{E,n+1}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme with structure morphism $a_B$. Use the ordered affine tower, coordinate Cartier boundaries of [def-pur-affine-space-coordinate-boundaries], and actual ordered supported cup product and its exceptional adjunct of [def-pur-affine-space-thom-map]. Let $C_r:Rz_{r,!}(A_B)\to W_r$ be this product in its compact-support source, as defined in [def-pur-coordinate-section-arrows]. Let $a_r:Rs_{r,!}(W_r)\to W_{r+1}$ be the last-coordinate Cartier arrow tensored with the pulled-back $W_r$, using the inverse specified proper projection and normalized Tate multiplication. Then $C_0$ is the specified compact-support identity. For every $r\in\mathbb N$, $C_{r+1}$ is the specified compact-support composition identification followed by $Rs_{r,!}(C_r)$ and $a_r$. Only the supported-arrow equations are asserted here; the exceptional-adjunct equations are not assumptions.

proof.text: Work first with ordinary etale witnesses, writing $Y=X_r$, $T=X_{r+1}$, $q=q_r$, $s=s_r$, $z=z_r$, $N=z_*A_B$, $R=s_*A_Y$ and $L=A_T(1)[2]$. Each coordinate is a nonzerodivisor over any base: multiplication by $t_i$ shifts polynomial coefficients injectively, and quotienting by any other coordinates leaves a polynomial ring. The inverse image of $V(t_i)$ under $q$ for $i\le r$ is the corresponding coordinate divisor on $T$. Their intersection with $s(Y)$ has ideal $(t_1,\ldots,t_{r+1})$ and is exactly $z_{r+1}(B)$. Thus every Cartier pullback used below is allowed. The finite twists are locally free rank one; in particular $q^*W_r$ is bounded constructible, of finite Tor amplitude, and the finite compact projection formula applies to $s$ with inputs $A_Y$ and $q^*W_r$.

proof.text:
Put $P=q^*N$, using the normalized closed-constant exchange, and put $\alpha=q^*C_r:P\to q^*W_r$. The supported cup pullback law and Cartier naturality identify the ordered product of the first $r$ coordinate factors on $T$ with this actual arrow $\alpha$, not just its source and target. In the cup definition let $\mu:P\otimes^L R\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*N=z_{r+1,*}A_B$ be restriction and multiplication on the intersection. Consequently the definition of the next ordered product is
$$C_{r+1}=m\circ(\alpha\otimes c_{s,A})\circ\mu^{-1},$$
where $m:q^*W_r\otimes L\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{r+1}$ is the specified shifted twist multiplication. This uses the same scheme-theoretic support transport as the Thom-map definition.

proof.text:
For an object $M$ on $Y$, denote by
$$\pi_M:R\otimes q^*M\longrightarrow s_*M$$
the counit-defined proper projection map, followed by $s^*q^*M=M$ and the tensor unitor. For $M=N$ all coefficient sources are flat degree-zero closed-constant sheaves. The map $\pi_N$ is exactly $\mu\circ\sigma$, where $\sigma:R\otimes P\to P\otimes R$ is symmetry: on any site object both maps restrict the two locally constant sections to the intersection and send $a\otimes b$ to $ab$. The counit in the definition of the projection map is restriction, so this also checks its normalization. The equality passes to the derived category using these same flat degree-zero models. Thus $\pi_N$ is invertible because $\mu$ is; no general projection-formula theorem for $N$ is needed.

proof.text:
Naturality of the counit-defined projection map in its second argument gives
$$\pi_{W_r}\circ(1_R\otimes\alpha)=s_*C_r\circ\pi_N.$$
Indeed substitute $q^*C_r$ into its defining pullback-tensor comparison and counit; their naturality gives this square, and $s^*q^*C_r=C_r$. The map $\pi_{W_r}$ is the specified projection isomorphism of Step 1. Substitute the square and $\pi_N=\mu\sigma$ into Step 2, moving $R$ to the first tensor position. This yields
$$C_{r+1}=m'\circ(c_{s,A}\otimes1)\circ\pi_{W_r}^{-1}\circ s_*C_r,$$
with $m':L\otimes q^*W_r\cong W_{r+1}$. The shift comparison in this reordering contributes $(-1)^{2\cdot2r}=1$; normalized Tate multiplication is the same on the two orders. This is precisely the displayed supported-map recursion in the statement, with its specified projection map.

proof.text: At c=0 the intersection, closed immersion and tensor unit are B, the identity of B and A_B, respectively. The Thom-map definition makes the empty product the identity. Cancelling its exceptional Hom bijection with the inverse in compactProduct, and applying the normalized proper closed comparison, gives the specified equality C_0 = coordinateIdentity.

theorem coordinate_supported_product_recursion (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (B : Scheme.{u}) (aB : B ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aB] [QuasiCompact aB] [IsSeparated aB] :
    compactProduct P n B aB 0 = coordinateIdentity P n B ∧
    (∀ r : ℕ, compactProduct P n B aB (r + 1) =
      (coordinateComposition P n B r).hom ≫
        (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (setting P n).Coefficient)
          (lastSection B r)).map (compactProduct P n B aB r) ≫ sectionArrow P n B aB r)
